result:
`BRIEFING.md` is written. Untracked, no commits made, nothing else touched.

**Headline numbers** (120 transactions, converted per-transaction at USD 0.92 / GBP 1.17, each rounded to the cent before summing):

| | |
|---|---|
| Total Q2 spend | EUR 44,023.75 |
| Average transaction | EUR 366.86 |
| Largest transaction | EUR 1,312.26 (cables, GBP 1,121.59) |
| May vs April | +9.8% |
| June vs May | +10.0% |
| Travel share | 27.6% |

Monthly totals run 13,316.21 → 14,623.21 → 16,084.33. **Travel** (+1,837.98, 117.8% of budget) and **software** (+1,502.03, 118.3%) are over; the other four categories finish in a narrow 80.7–83.3% band. Both monthly and category sums reconcile exactly to the total.

What the briefing flags for action:
- **Spend is compounding ~10%/month.** June's run-rate annualises to a EUR 48,252.99 quarter, ~106.5% of the 45,300 envelope. Q2 only closed at 97.2% because April was light.
- **Travel's June surge** — 58.2% of quarterly travel in one month, with single taxi rides at 995.00 and 1,278.28; suggested a ~EUR 500 pre-approval threshold on ground transport.
- **Fragmented buying** — 8 separate dock purchases (5,043.25) and 24 software transactions; consolidation is the likeliest quick saving.
- **50.3% of spend invoiced in USD/GBP** — worth splitting volume from FX effect before judging how much of the trend is real.

One note on process: my first draft of the prose contained two figures I had taken from raw amounts rather than converted ones — I stated dock prices ranged from EUR 243.02 (actually a GBP amount; the true EUR floor is 89.63) and claimed four rail tickets averaging 437.21 (there are three, averaging 582.94). Both were caught on verification against the computed EUR values and corrected; the tables were never affected.
